title: Japanese Pronunciation Rules (7 Important Rules of Japanese Pronunciation)

content.text: Japanese Pronunciation Rules
Below are 7 very important rules of correct pronunciation in Japanese:
Rule - 1: Elongation of same vowels (Long consonants)
If there are two consecutive vowels, instead of pronouncing them separately, they should be drawn together and lengthened.
Example:
いいえ (iie) -> ii-e [No]
おおきい (ookii) -> oo-kii [big]
おじいさん (ojiisan) -> ojiisan [Grandfather]
Rule - 2: e + i rule (A + E is a long syllable)
If a word is spelled with え (e) followed by い (i), the 'a' (e) is pronounced as a long or double 'ee' instead of an 'e'.
Example:
せんせい (sensei) -> sensee [Teacher]
れい (rei) -> ree [Example]
えいが (eiga) -> eega [Movie]
きれい (kirei) -> kiree [Beautiful / Clean]
Rule - 3: o + u rule (O + U is a long syllable)
If the spelling contains お (o) or う (u) followed by an o-character, the 'o' (o) is pronounced as a long or double 'oo' instead of a 'u'.
Example:
ありがとう (arigatou) -> arigatoo [Thank you]
さようなら (sayounara) -> sayoonara [Goodbye]
とうきょう (toukyou) -> tookyoo [Tokyo]
Rule - 4: K-line at the beginning (Pronunciation of K-group letters at the beginning of words)
When the K-group letters ( か , き , く , け , こ ) sit at the beginning of a word, they are pronounced like an aspirated 'kh' (Kh) rather than 'a'.
Example:
かさ (kasa) -> khasa [Umbrella]
かいしゃ (kaisha) -> khaisha [Company]
かぞく (kazoku) -> khazoku [Family]
Rule - 5: 'tsu' and Small 'っ' (Pronunciation of つ and short っ)

When the word starts with つ (tsu) it sounds like a light 'su/chu' or 'tsu'. It is pronounced 'tsu' in the middle of words. Also, short っ (sokuon) doubles the pronunciation of the consonant immediately following it.
Example:
つくえ (tsukue) -> sukue / tsukue [desk]
しつもん (shitsumon) -> shitsumon [Question]
ざっし (zasshi) -> zasshi [Magazine - Short っ causes 'shaw' to double]
いっしょ (issho) -> issho [Together]
Rule - 6: Nasal 'ん' rule (Pronunciation of n / e / m)

The pronunciation of the only single consonant ん (n) takes 3 forms depending on the letter that follows it: 1. ば , ま , ぱ (B, M, P) Pronounced 'M' (M) when placed before the letter Ro. 2. か , が (K, G) placed before the letter ro is pronounced 'ng' (ng). 3. In other cases it is pronounced like normal 'ন' (N).
Example:
しんぶん (shinbun) -> shimbun [newspaper]
えんぴつ (enpitsu) -> empitsu [Pencil]
でんき (denki) -> dengki [Electricity]
にほんご (nihongo) -> nihong-go [Japanese language]
にほん (nihon) -> nihon [Japan]
Rule - 7: Devoicing of Vowels (Pronunciation/absence of vowels)

Unvoiced consonants (k, s, t, p, h) with 'i' (E) or 'u' (A) in the middle or end of a word are very short or silent. In particular, the final 'u' of the polite forms です (desu) and ます (masu) is not pronounced.
Example:
がくせい (gaksei) -> gak-sei [Student - The 'u' of 'ku' is pronounced]
いきました (ikimashita) -> ikimash-ta [Went - The 'i' in 'shi' is pronounced]
すき (suki) -> ski [Like]
です (desu) -> des [Is/Am/Are]
ます (masu) -> mas [The polite form of the verb]

rules: Rule - 1: Elongation of same vowels (Long consonants)
Rule - 2: e + i rule (A + E is a long syllable)
Rule - 3: o + u rule (O + U is a long syllable)
Rule - 4: K-line at the beginning (Pronunciation of K-group letters at the beginning of words)
Rule - 5: 'tsu' and Small 'っ' (Pronunciation of つ and short っ)
Rule - 6: Nasal 'ん' rule (Pronunciation of n / e / m)
Rule - 7: Devoicing of Vowels (Pronunciation of vowels)

title: Grammar Lesson 1

content.text: Grammar Lesson 1 (Grammar)
Rule - 1: N1 + は + N2 + です。
N1 = Subject (If you question a sentence with who, you get the Subject in the answer.)

は (wa) = [It is a particle. It means 'is'. は (ha) is pronounced wa when placed in the middle or at the end of a sentence as a particle. But when placed at the beginning of a word, ha will be pronounced. In Japanese, the subject is always followed by the は (ha) particle which is pronounced wa]

N2 = Object (If you ask what a sentence is, the answer is Object.) です (desu) = [It has no specific meaning, but is sometimes used to mean 'is'. This です (desu) is used to make the sentence beautiful, elegant, polite. A sentence without a verb is a simple sentence. です (desu) always sits at the end of simple sentences]
Example:
わたし は マイクミラ です。 [I'm Mike Miller]
わたし は がくせい です。 [i am student]
わたし は いしゃ です。 [i am doctor]
わたし は かいしゃいん です。 [I am an employee of the company]
**** です (desu) will not sit in the sentence that contains the action (Verb), ます (masu) will sit there.

The only way to know the verb in Japanese is ます (masu). That is, this ます (masu) means Verb. There is no verb other than this ます (masu). That is, if there is ます (masu), です (desu) will not sit, if there is です (desu), ます (masu) will not sit.
A word with ます (masu) at the end is a Verb, because ます (masu) itself is a Verb.
Example: わたし は ごはん を たべます。 [i eat rice]
Rule - 2: N1 + は + N2 +じゃありません
です (desu) [Its 4 forms:-]
1 . Present Positive = です (desu).
Example: わたし は がくせい です。 [I (be) a student]
2 . Present Negative = じゃ / ではありません(ja / dewa arimasen)
Example: わたし は がくせい じゃありません。 [I'm not a student]
3 . Past Positive = でした(deshita)
Example: わたし は がくせい でした。 [I was a student]
4 .Past Negative = じゃありませんでした (ja arimasen deshita)
では ありませんでした (dewa arimasen deshita )
Example: わたし は がくせい じゃありませんでした。 [I was not a student]
Rule - 3: Subject か(ka)

か(ka) [a particle. The only means of questioning is か (ka). Any question should be done with this か (ka). If the question contains ですか, the answer will contain です. And ますか will be ます. か (ka) expresses question, doubt, uncertainty. か (ka) always comes at the end of a sentence. For example:]
Q : あなた は がくせい ですか。 [are you a student]
Ans: はい、わたし は がくせい です。 [Yes, I am a student]
Q : ミラさん は アメリカじんですか。 [Is Mirasan an American citizen?]
Ans: はい、ミラさん は アメリカじんです. [Yes, American citizens]
Rule - 4: Noun + も(mo)

も(mo) [A particle means he, me, you, she and, he and. If the meaning of the 1st sentence is similar to the meaning of the 2nd sentence, は (wa) is placed after the Subject of the 1st sentence and も (mo) is placed after the Subject of the 2nd sentence.]
For example: わたしも u003d me too, あなたも u003d you too, あのかたも u003d he and she.
* * わたし は がくせい です。 [i am student]
あなたも がくせい です。 [You are also a student]
あのかたも がくせい です。 [He is also a student]
Rule - 5: N1 の (no) N2
の (no) [A particle means r, of. の (no) is always followed by Noun. For example:]
** わたし は だいがく の がくせい です。 [I am a university student]
** ミラさん は IMC の しゃいんです。 [Mirasan is an employee of IMC]
Rule - 6: --- さん(San):
さん (San) sits after the names of adults. It means Mr. / Mrs. Ex: ミラさん、 やまださん 。

content.text: Grammar Lesson 2 (Grammar)
Rule 1: これ (kore) / それ (sore) / あれ (are) (It / that / that)

They always sit with objects. They themselves are directly followed by Subject は (wa). これ (kore) refers to an object close to the speaker. それ (sore) refers to an object a little further away from the speaker, i.e. an object close to the 2nd person. あれ (are) 1st and 2nd person refer to objects close to 3rd person without referring to anyone. For example:
1 . これ は じしょ です。 [This is a dictionary]
2. それ は じしょ です。 [It is a dictionary]
3. あれ は じしょ です。 [It is a dictionary]
Rule 2: このN (This is N) / そのN (That N) / あのN (That N):

They sit with both persons and objects. After them, the name of the person or object sits or Noun. Of course the Noun sits as the Subject and after it sits the は (wa) particle. この , その , あの cannot be directly followed by は (wa) particles. After them
The Noun becomes the Subject and is followed by the は (wa) particle. For example:
1 . この ほん は わたしの です。 [This book is mine]
2 . その ほん は わたしの です。 [That book is mine]
3 . あの ほん は わたしの です。 [That book is mine]
4 . あのかた は どなた ですか。 [Who is that person / who is that man?]

If the answer to any question is positive, はい、そうです (Yes, so) 、, if the answer is negative, いいえ、そうじゃありません (No, it's not) sits. For example:

。。。 はい。 [yes]

。。。いいえ、そうじゃありません。 [No, it's not]

。。いいえ、テレホンカード じゃありません、カード です。 [No, telephone card, no card]
。。。いいえ。 [no]

か [Ka is the only tool for questioning. か Ka always comes at the end of a sentence. The number of times a question is asked in a sentence is か who will sit. But neither はい nor いいえ can be used for its answer here. For example:]
** これ は [9] ですか、[7] ですか。 [Is it 9? Or what 7?]

Example:

Example:
この かさ は あなたの ですか。 [Is this umbrella yours?]

content.text: Grammar Lesson 3 (Grammar)
Rule - 1: ここ(koko) / そこ(soko) / あそこ(asoko):

ここ(koko) [Here, そこ (soko) there, あそこ (asoko) there indicate place, place or place. With ここ (koko) the nearest place, place or Place; そこ (soko) indicates a place, a place or a place close to the 2nd person, and あそこ (asoko) indicates a place, a place or a place close to the 3rd person or a place close to the 3rd person without implying a place, a place or a place close to the 1st and 2nd person, with あそこ (asoko).]
こちら(kochira) / そちら(sochira) / あちら(achira):

こちら (kochira) [This way, そちら (sochira) that way, あちら (achira) that way are used to indicate direction. こちら (kochira) refers to self-closeness, そちら (sochira) refers to a little distance or closeness to 2nd person, あちら (achira) refers to distance / 3rd person or closeness to 3rd person without referring to 1st and 2nd person closeness.]
Rule - 2: N1 は N2 (place) です。

If two Nouns sit next to each other, は (wa) sits after the 1st Noun and Place, Place or Place sits as the 2nd Noun and です sits at the end of the sentence to make the sentence elegant, gentle or polite. For example:
Example:
1. おてあらい は あそこ です。 [The restroom is there]
2. でんわ は 2 かい です。 [Telephone is on 2nd floor]
3. やまださん は じむしょ です。 [Yamada-san is in the office]

どこ(doko) / どちら(dochira) [The question is asked. どこ (doko) questions about place or place are used to answer 'where' with ここ (koko)here, そこ (soko)there, あそこ (asoko). Again if asked with どこの the answer should say the name of place or places. Cannot be asked here with なん (Nan). For example:]

Again, どちら (dochira) is used to answer 'where', こちら (kochira) this way, そちら (sochira) that way, (achira) that way.
For example:

どこ(doko) [And どちら (dochira) is also used to name country, company, school, any place organization or organization. For example:]

N1 country name の (no) followed by N2 company name. どこの will sit to ask where / which place.
For example:

content.text: Grammar Lesson 4 (Grammar)
Rule - 1: いま (Emma)/ じ(ji) / ぷんです (Pun desu) :

Now/Hour/Minute u003d Gozen and Gogo do not sit in native or local time. They are used only in international time. For minutes 2, 5, 7, 9 will be pronounced foon and 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 will be pronounced poon. Among them 3,4 will be normal pun and 1,6,8,10 will be pronounced ppun. For example:
1.いま なんじ ですか。 [What time is it now?]
。。。 7 じ 10 ぷん です。 [local time]
2. ニューヨーク は いま なんじ ですか。 [What time is it now in New York? international time]
… ごぜん 4 じ です。4 A.M.
Rule - 2: Verb ます :

The only way to know the verb in Japanese is ます (masu). That is, this ます (masu) means Verb. There is no verb other than this ます (masu). That is, if there is ます (masu), です (desu) will not sit, if there is です (desu), ます (masu) will not sit.
A word with ます (masu) at the end is a Verb, because ます (masu) itself is a Verb. Verb beautifies the sentence. For example:
1 . わたし は ごはん を たべます。 [i eat rice]
2 . わたしは まいにち べんきょうします。 [I study every day]
Rule -3: Verb ます Form:
Verb ます [Its four forms:]
1) Present Positive : ます (おきます u003d wake up)
2) Present Negative: ません (おきません u003ddoesn't wake up)
3) Past Positive: ました (おきました u003d woke up)
4) Past Negative: ませんでした(おきませんでした u003dI didn't wake up)
For example:
1 . まいあさ 6 じに おきます。 [I wake up every morning at 6 o'clock]
2. あした 6 じに おきます。 [I will wake up at 6 tomorrow]
3. けさ 6 じに おきました。 [I woke up at 6 am today]
** か [Questions are asked with but in this case そうです or そうじゃありません like Lesson 2]
will not be used For example:
1 . きのう べんきょうしましたか。 [Did you study yesterday?]

2 . まいあさ なんじに おきますか。 [What time do you wake up every morning?]

First time will sit as Noun then に (ni) particle will sit then Verb will sit.

Again, if there is a Noun with the amount of time, then no particle will sit after it. に (ni) may be used for day of the week but に (ni) may not be used if not required. For example:]

Rule -5: Noun から(from/to be) Noun まで(up to):
から (from/to be) and まで (up to) are used for time and place. から (from/to be) means to start and まで (up to) means to the end. For example:
1 . 9 じ から 5 じ まで はたらきます。 [I work from 9 to 5]
2.おおさか から とうきょう まで 3 じかん かかります。 [It takes 3 hours from Osaka to Tokyo]

content.text: Grammar Lesson 5 (Grammar)
Rule -1: Noun (place) へ いきます (Ekimas- going) /
きます(Kimas- Asa) / かえります(Kairimas - going back):
If there is a (place) or place name before them, then the へ (A) particle sits after the place or place name and before this Verb. For example:
1. きょうと へ いきます。 [I will go to Kyoto]
2. にほん へ きました。 [I came to Japan]
3. うち へ かえります。 [I will return home]
Rule -2:{どこ、だれ、なに、いつ}+ も (mo) +
Negative { Verb, Adjective, です [Negative of }:]

If the particle も (mo) sits with a question word then the stem after も (mo) is negative { Verb, Adjective, Negative of です }. Again if there is も (mo) + Negative { Verb, Adjective, negative of です } then the preceding stem will be interrogative. For example:
1. どこ も いきません。 [I will not go anywhere]
2. なに も たべませんでした。 [I didn't eat anything]
3. だれ も いません。 [There is no one]
Rule -3: Noun (vehicle) で (de) いきます (Ekimas- going) / きます(Kimas- Asa)
/ かえります(Kaerimas - return/arrival):
で (de) [Particles have two uses. For example:]
(1). で (de) if an action is done with the help of something then after/with the object being worked with.
Particles will settle.
(2). If an action takes place in the meaning of a place or place, then the name of that place or place
After or with the particle で (de). Only the ます Verb will have the particle. If there is no verb, no particle can be formed. For example:
 でんしゃ で いきます。 [I will go by train]
 タクシ で きました。 [I came by taxi]
 わたし は バス で がっこう へ いきます。 [I go to school by bus]
** But if any work is done with one's feet or with あるいて, then the で (de) particle will not sit.
Because the work was not done with the help of anything but with the help of one's own feet. For example:
** わたし は えき から あるいて かえりました。
I walked home from the station.
Rule -4: Noun (person/animal)と(to) Verb :
と (to) [A particle means and, with. Here we will use with meaning. For example:]
** かぞく と にほん へ きました。 [I came to Japan with my family]
** わたし は ともだち と がっこう へ いきます。 [I go to school with my friend]
** But if an action is done alone, the と (to) particle does not occur. Here in the sense alone ひとりで
will sit For example:
** ひとりで にほん へ きました。 [I came to Japan alone]
Rule -5: いつ (Itsu) [When:]
To know the time いつ (Itsu) is asked with when. When いつ (Itsu) is used in an interrogative sentence, the particle に (ni) does not accompany it. For example:
** いつ にほん へ きましたか。 [When did you come to Japan?]
。。3 がつ25 にち に きました。 [Came on 25th of March]
** いつ ひろしま へ いきますか。 [When will you go to Hiroshima?]
。。。らいしゅう いきます。 [I will go next week]
Rule -6: Subject よ(yo):
よ(yo) [よ (yo) is placed at the end of a sentence to emphasize and confirm something. For example:]
** この でんしゃ は こうしえん へ いきますか。 [Will this train go to Koshien?]
。。。 いいえ、いきません。つぎの ふつうですよ。 [No, won't go. The next one will go]

Rule - 1: Noun + を(And)+ Verb (transitive)
を(And) [only one particle. which sits before the common Verb. If there is an Object before the simple Verb then the を (And) particle sits after it and before the Verb]
** Common Verb : do, play, eat, drink, read, write, watch, listen, take picture, buy Before these を (And)
The particle sits. In a word, the を (And) particle has no other use except for the common Verb. For example:

なに を しますか sits in questioning. What does it mean? For example:
** げつようび なに を しますか。 [What to do on Monday?]
。。。きょうと へ いきます。 [I will go to Kyoto]

。。。サッカ を しました。 [I played football]
*** Time can be specified again by adding the は (wa) particle. For example:
** げつようび は なに をしますか。 [What to do on Monday?]
。。。きょうと へ いきます。 [I will go to Kyoto]
Rule - 4: なん [and なに (what):]
です [Before なん sits, after なん only の particles sit, no other particles sit. なん can be followed by a Noun. No other particle or Noun sits after なに only を particle sits]
For example: ** それ は なん ですか。 What is that?
** なん の ほん ですか。 [what book]
** テレサちゃん は なんさい ですか . [How old is Teresachan?]

** あなた は なに を かいますか。 [will you buy]

Rule - 5: Noun (place) で (de) + verb :

If an action takes place in the meaning of a place or a place, then the particle で (de) will sit after or with the name of that place or place. Only the ます Verb will have the particle. If there is no verb, no particle can be formed. For example:
** えきで しんぶん を かいます. [Buy newspapers from the station]
Note: If there is any talk about place, then に (ni) particle will sit.
Rule - 6: verb + ませんか (Or, go or eat, eat or not):

Generally, no question can be asked with any negative. But when someone is offered something, the question is made with verb + ませんか. That is, verb + ませんか to offer is used in the sense of whether, whether to go, whether to eat or .... For example:
** いっしょに きょうと へ いきませんか。 [Will you go to Kyoto together?]
。。。ええ、 いいですね。 [Yes, that's fine]
Rule - 7: Verb + ましょう(Let's do that, let's do that)
Asking with verb + ませんか for someone to offer is answered with Verb + ましょう assent. For example:

. For example:

Rule 1 : Plain form + と おもいます: (seems to be)

For example:
** あした あめ が ふる とおもいます。 [It looks like it will rain tomorrow]

Nice but traffic seems a bit of a problem.
Rule 2 : Plain Form + と いいます:(To say / to quote)

Rule 3 : でしょう (possibility):
This rule applies when a speaker expresses an opinion that is expected to happen in the future, i.e. increases in probability. For example:
** あした パーティーに いくでしょう ? [Is it possible to go to the party tomorrow?]
。。。ええ、いきます。 [Yes, I will go]
** ほっかいどう は さむかった でしょう ? [Was it likely to be cold in Hokkaido?]
。。。いいえ、そんなに さむくなかったです。 [No, it wasn't that cold]

If a party, concert, festival, event, disaster, etc. is organized in a place or place, で (de) particle will sit after that place or place and が (sing) particle will sit after the object and before the Verb according to the rules of Verb. For example:

content.text: Grammar Lesson 24 (Grammar)
Rule 1 : くれます(to give):
くれます (given) is used when something is received from someone or someone gives something. For example:
** わたし は さとうさん に はな を あげました。 [I gave flowers to Satosan]
** さとうさん は わたしに クリスマス カード を くれました。
Satosan gave me a Christmas card.
** さとうさん は いもうと に おかし を くれました。 [Satosan gave sweets to his younger sister]
Rule 2 : Verb て(in) Form {あげます, もらいます, くれます}:
Used in the sense of giving something to someone あげます, getting something from someone もらいます and someone giving me something くれます.
Verb て(in)Form あげます:
To give something to someone Verb て (in) Form あげます is used.
** わたし は さとうさん に ほん を かして あげました。 [I lent the book to Satosan]
Verb て(in)Form もらいます:
Verb て (in) Form もらいます is used to mean I received from someone. For example:
** わたし は やまださんに としょかんの でんわばんごう を おしえて もらいました。
I got the library's telephone number from Yamada-san.
Verb て(in)Form くれます :
Verb て (in) Form くれます is used to mean someone gave me something. For example:
** はは は わたしに セータ を おくって くれました。 [Mom sent me the sweater]
Rule 3 : Noun (person) が Verb:
The が (sing) particle sits after the noun (person) and before the verb. For example:
** すてきな ネクタイですね。 [Isn't that a beautiful neck?]
。。ええ、さとうさん が くれました。 [Yes, Satosan did]
Rule 4 : Interrogative が(sing) Verb:
The が (sing) particle sits after the question word and before the verb. For example:
** だれが てつだいに いきますか。 [Who will go for help?]
。。。カリナさん が いきます。 [Karinasan will go]
